card.name: Zar
card.era: documented in southern Iran from the 19th century (African diaspora origins)
card.tagline: Afro-Iranian spirit-possession healing ritual of the Persian Gulf coast
card.profile: Zar (Zar) in southern Iran is a ritual healing and spirit-negotiation practice of the Afro-Iranian communities of the Persian Gulf coast, especially Hormozgan, Bandar Abbas and Qeshm Island (Encyclopaedia Iranica). 'Bad' (wind) is the general term for possessing spirits, and 'zar' refers to the most dangerous winds - believed to come from Africa - as well as the ritual used to engage and pacify them (Project MUSE; Iranica). Led by a Baba Zar or Mama Zar, the ceremony uses drumming, incantations sung in mixed Persian, Arabic, Swahili and Indian, incense and rhythmic movement until the possessed person responds to the specific beat of their spirit (Encyclopaedia Iranica). It is a healing/adorcism practice, not entertainment.
card.insight: The Iranian zar is part of the wider Zar cult of the Red Sea and East Africa, spread through the Indian Ocean slave trade; in DSM-IV it was listed as a culture-bound syndrome (Iranian Journal of Psychiatry, NCBI).
card.image_significance: Spirit-possession healing ritual — not entertainment. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — S. coast, Iran.
